inputs.original_text: John Lahart is right that inheritance tax rules shouldn’t treat people without children as less deserving of fairness. But reform must challenge the wider inequality built into inheritance itself, not create another advantage for those able to pass wealth to relatives. A fair system should respect different family structures while making sure inherited privilege doesn’t deepen inequality or drain resources needed by everyone.
inputs.modified_text: John Lahart is right that people without children should not be treated as less deserving of fairness. But that cannot become a pretext to weaken the right of families to pass on what they have worked to build. Inheritance is more than privilege: it is a way parents and relatives support the next generation and preserve a family’s security. A fair system should respect different family circumstances without turning every family legacy into an excuse for greater state control or redistribution.
